app.title: QR-Todo
app.tagline: Hand a list to someone standing next to you — no internet needed.

transfer.showBack: Show this back to them so they can finish.

networkConfig.label: Network config
networkConfig.description: Validates the configured browser-reachable relay addresses and prepares the libp2p transports and services.

libp2p.label: libp2p
libp2p.description: Creates and starts the libp2p node, including its peer identity, discovery, relay, WebSocket and WebRTC support.

helia.label: Helia
helia.description: Starts the Helia IPFS node on top of libp2p and enables block exchange.

orbitdb.label: OrbitDB
orbitdb.description: Loads or creates the OrbitDB identity and initialises OrbitDB using the Helia node.

databaseSync.label: Database + sync
databaseSync.description: Opens the todo database, loads its local operation log and starts OrbitDB pubsub synchronisation.

localTodos.label: Local todos
localTodos.description: Connects the local todo store and starts filling it from OrbitDB in the background.

relayConnected.label: Relay connected
relayConnected.description: A live connection to a relay.

peerConnected.label: Peer connected
peerConnected.description: A live libp2p connection to another browser.

webrtcConnected.label: WebRTC connected
webrtcConnected.description: A direct WebRTC connection to another browser.

lists.shareAddress: Share this address so others can open the list. They can read it right away; writing needs a grant below.

simple.lead: You have a list, and somebody next to you needs it. You hold up a code, their phone reads it with its camera — done.
simple.offline: No internet needed. The list goes straight from one device to the other.
simple.hotspot: The two devices do have to be on the same network. If they are not, one of them opens a Wi-Fi hotspot and the other joins it.
simple.passkey: A passkey is your signature. It shows the other side that the entries came from you. You can use the app without one.

tech.heading: Why it sometimes fails on a mobile network
tech.nat: Mobile networks commonly use symmetric NAT, which defeats exactly the direct connection the code sets up.
tech.chromeIpv6: Chrome does not surface IPv6 WebRTC candidates, so the path that would otherwise work on a mobile network is not offered at all.
tech.browsers: DuckDuckGo and Safari pass IPv6 candidates reliably. One caveat: DuckDuckGo may not support passkeys on Android or GrapheneOS.
tech.graphene: Vanadium on GrapheneOS works well with WebRTC enabled in the security settings — and, if you use passkeys, Passchain from Accrescent installed.
tech.vpn: If both devices are on mobile data, a VPN such as NymVPN gets you past the NAT.

check.heading: This device, right now
check.none: Your network offers no path out over IPv4 or IPv6.
check.sameNetwork: If you are on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot as the other device, none of this matters and it works anyway.
check.routable: Your network allows a direct connection even to devices on other networks.
check.localOnly: Your network assigns a new port per destination (symmetric NAT). That will not reach a device on another network.

relay.label: Connect through a relay
relay.hint: Off by default: this app needs no server. Tick it only if the other device cannot scan your code — over a messenger, for instance.

relay.none: No relay answered. The code path still works; you can start your own relay.

ways.heading: How the other device gets in
ways.qr: By camera: you hold up a code, they scan it. Nothing leaves this network.
